clue.text: Singer's favourite set in Warsaw

parts.note: Isaac Bashevis Singer's novel named after the narrator's childhood sweetheart, a girl from Krochmalna Street in Warsaw

explanation.surface: A singer's favourite song is performed in the Polish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist; it is the Nobel-winning Yiddish novelist Isaac Bashevis Singer, whose novel bears the heroine's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Singer's novel is the narrator's beloved, living in Warsaw before the war.

clue.text: Useful guides for Two on a Tower

definitions.text: Useful guides for Two on a Tower

parts.words: Useful guides for Two on a Tower
parts.note: Two on a Tower is Thomas Hardy's novel about a young astronomer observing from a tower, so his guides would be charts of the night sky

explanation.surface: A couple up a tower need something to help them find their way.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts of the constellations are what an astronomer in Hardy's novel would consult while watching the heavens.

clue.text: For him, tragically, love leads to hell inside

definitions.text: For him, tragically, love leads to hell inside

indicators.note: leads says the first piece comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, giving the letter O

indicators.note: inside says one word is placed within the other

explanation.surface: For one tragic hero, love brings him to an inner hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' and 'leads' place the pieces; read whole, the clue also describes Shakespeare's Moor, whose love for his wife ends in torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor is driven by jealousy of his beloved wife into a private torment, so the whole clue describes his tragedy.

clue.text: Name of section, like Bede or Lear

definitions.meaning: a short title printed on its own page before a section or the main title page of a book
Bede is half of the title Adam Bede and Lear half of King Lear

explanation.walkthrough: Bede and Lear look like the historian and the nonsense poet; they are each one half of a famous title.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers use this term for the short title printed alone before a book's main title page or a part; Bede and Lear are each half a famous title.

clue.text: I led prom unbelievable as it may be, earnestly requested

indicators.note: something unbelievable is beyond reason, so these letters are put into a new, improbable order

explanation.surface: Someone begged, however incredible it sounds, that I had run the school prom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbelievable as it may be' reworks the letters of I LED PROM.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or beseech someone is to ask them earnestly for something.

clue.text: She was "able to do anything from a medley dance to Lady Macbeth "

definitions.text: She was "able to do anything from a medley dance to Lady Macbeth "

parts.words: She was "able to do anything from a medley dance to Lady Macbeth "
parts.note: a quotation from Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby describing the versatile actress in Mr Crummles's touring company

explanation.surface: A versatile performer who could manage everything from a dance medley to Shakespearean tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's actress in the Crummles theatrical company is praised for exactly this range of stage parts.

clue.text: Some strong desires of Clark Blaise

definitions.meaning: the Canadian-American writer Clark Blaise published a novel with this title in 1983

explanation.walkthrough: 'of Clark Blaise' looks like a hidden word in his name, but it is a book title of his.
explanation.definitionFit: Cravings are intense wants, and the same word is the title of a novel by Clark Blaise.

clue.text: Huxley's Lawrence disguised in a bellflower

definitions.meaning: in Aldous Huxley's Point Counter Point
a campanula species grown for its edible root

explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' looks like an anagram signal; it means Lawrence appears under another name in Huxley's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The campanula with edible roots shares its name with Huxley's fictional version of D. H. Lawrence.

clue.text: Italian poet's count

definitions.meaning: belonging to the author of the Divine Comedy, written with an apostrophe
Edmond, Dumas's hero, becomes the Count of Monte Cristo

explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a verb or number; it is the title of Dumas's hero Edmond.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of the Florentine poet's name is spelt like the surname of Dumas's Count of Monte Cristo.

clue.text: … certainly the most efficient - - — fliers that ever appeared. They were the invention of a Japanese artist" (H. G. Wells, The War in the Air)

definitions.text: … certainly the most efficient - - — fliers that ever appeared. They were the invention of a Japanese artist" (H. G. Wells, The War in the Air)

parts.words: … certainly the most efficient - - — fliers that ever appeared. They were the invention of a Japanese artist" (H. G. Wells, The War in the Air)
parts.note: a quotation from H. G. Wells's novel about aerial war; the gap holds the term for flying machines denser than the atmosphere, as opposed to airships

explanation.surface: A quotation praising Japanese-designed flying machines in an early science-fiction war.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeroplanes, unlike balloons and airships, are craft denser than the atmosphere they fly through.

clue.text: Greek hero protects university for self-styled emperor

indicators.note: protects suggests one word wrapped around another to shield it

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek warrior defends a college on behalf of a pretender to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman usurper who proclaimed himself ruler in Egypt around 297 AD had this name.

clue.text: Dramatist and pure dramatic character

definitions.meaning: Neil, the American playwright of The Odd Couple
... Pure is a character in Susanna Centlivre's comedy A Bold Stroke for a Wife, whose name came to mean the genuine article

explanation.walkthrough: 'pure' looks like an adjective; it is the surname of Centlivre's Quaker character.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil the playwright shares the name with Centlivre's Quaker, the first half of Simon Pure.

clue.text: "A 500-pound incendiary something like the old Russian — Breadbasket" (Ted Lawson, Thirty Seconds over Tokyo)

definitions.text: "A 500-pound incendiary something like the old Russian — Breadbasket" (Ted Lawson, Thirty Seconds over Tokyo)

parts.words: "A 500-pound incendiary something like the old Russian — Breadbasket" (Ted Lawson, Thirty Seconds over Tokyo)
parts.note: a quotation from Ted Lawson's memoir of the Doolittle Raid; the gap holds the Soviet foreign minister's name given to a cluster bomb used in the Winter War

explanation.surface: A wartime pilot describes a firebomb by comparison with a Soviet weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet cluster incendiary of 1939-40 was nicknamed after the foreign minister Vyacheslav, as was the petrol-bomb cocktail.

clue.text: Verse form from palimpsest in Egyptian library

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A poem's form found on an overwritten scroll in an Alexandrian library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the answer out of palimpsEST IN Egyptian; 'library' only dresses the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-stanza poem with recurring line-end words is a fixed lyric pattern, and this is one spelling of its name.

clue.text: The "honour of the house" was his weak point, and Stalky and Co. knew how to flick him on the raw

definitions.text: The "honour of the house" was his weak point, and Stalky and Co. knew how to flick him on the raw

parts.words: The "honour of the house" was his weak point, and Stalky and Co. knew how to flick him on the raw
parts.note: describes the earnest housemaster whom Kipling's schoolboy trio torment in Stalky and Co.

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's pride in his boarding house made him an easy target for pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's housemaster, obsessed with his house's reputation, is the chief victim of Stalky and his friends.

clue.text: Bathsheba, always with strange need

indicators.note: strange says the letters of the next word come out oddly arranged

explanation.surface: The biblical Bathsheba is forever paired with an odd kind of want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges NEED as DENE; Bathsheba is Hardy's heroine in Far from the Madding Crowd, not the biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's heroine in Far from the Madding Crowd bears this surname, so her first name identifies it.

clue.text: Betrayed wife shows spirit in new edition of Sade

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
a new edition reworks a text, so the letters of the following name are rearranged

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit

explanation.surface: A deceived wife appears devilish in a fresh printing of the Marquis's works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new edition of' rearranges the Marquis's name to DESA, and 'in' puts the spirit inside it; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife is falsely accused through Iago's treachery, making her the wronged spouse of the play.

clue.text: It offers the conclusion in which nothing is concluded

definitions.text: It offers the conclusion in which nothing is concluded

parts.words: It offers the conclusion in which nothing is concluded
parts.note: Samuel Johnson's philosophical tale ends with a chapter titled The Conclusion, in which Nothing is Concluded

explanation.surface: A book whose ending refuses to settle anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's tale of the Abyssinian prince closes with a final chapter famously titled this way.

clue.text: Lord Clonbrony, for example

parts.note: the Irish landowner in Maria Edgeworth's novel who lives in London away from his estates

explanation.surface: An Irish peer offered as a typical case.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Clonbrony is in Maria Edgeworth's novel of that title, an Irish landlord who neglects his estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgeworth's peer is a landlord living away from his property, which is also the title of her novel.

clue.text: On account of preceding the dark hours in Ellroy's work

definitions.text: preceding the dark hours in Ellroy's work
definitions.meaning: James Ellroy's novel is titled ___ the Night, so this word comes before 'the Night'

explanation.walkthrough: 'the dark hours' stands for 'the Night' in the title of James Ellroy's 1984 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction giving a reason means for the reason that, and opens the title of Ellroy's novel.

clue.text: Such stress can be grave, or even acute

definitions.text: Such stress can be grave, or even acute

parts.words: Such stress can be grave, or even acute
parts.note: reads like a medical warning about worry, but grave and acute are marks placed over letters

explanation.surface: A doctor's warning that some kinds of strain may be serious or severe.

explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis on a syllable is a kind of stress, and the grave and acute are written marks of that name.

clue.text: Burney heiress

parts.note: the title heroine of Fanny Burney's 1782 novel, a young woman who inherits a fortune on condition her husband takes her surname

explanation.surface: A rich young woman from a novelist's pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanny Burney's second novel is named after its heiress heroine, Miss Beverley.

clue.text: Anthem composer suggests twisted yarn

a fine, tightly twisted cotton thread used for stockings

explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story; it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of La Marseillaise is Rouget de ___, and the same word is a smooth, hard-twisted cotton thread.

clue.text: Real set surprisingly seen in Hamlet film

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A genuine film set unexpectedly spotted in a screen version of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius's son, who duels with the prince at the end, is a character appearing in every version of the play.

clue.text: Roman horse on stage

definitions.meaning: Peter Shaffer's 1973 play about a boy who blinds horses

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for horse is also the title of Peter Shaffer's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for horse is also the title of Peter Shaffer's stage drama about a disturbed stable boy.

clue.text: Our Altaic version of the author

explanation.surface: Someone presents their own rendering of a Central Asian language family belonging to a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to a writer, from the Latin for originator.
